title: Knowledge Artifact
content:
# Knowledge Artifact

> **2026-07-17 reconciliation note:** this spec's original design called for GitHub Packages
> (Maven, `com.manetu` groupId) and `sentence-transformers`/`bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d) embeddings.
> The shipped implementation (`de42350`, `5a48cc9`, `fa80b98`) deliberately diverged on both points
> — see "Publishing" and "Implementation" below for the actual, current design. The BM25
> serialization format below was already updated post-implementation and is accurate as written.

## Introduction

A new GitHub Actions workflow in github.com/manetu/policyengine runs on each MPE release
tag and publishes a single versioned package: `mpe-knowledge-vX.Y.Z`.

### Build steps (run in GH Actions only; not part of the Go build)

1. Walk `docs/docs/`, split each `.md` at H2 boundaries (and at code-fence boundaries
   within an H2 if the section is large), capture
   `{path, heading_path[], frontmatter, text}`.
2. Generate dense embeddings via a local Ollama server running `nomic-embed-text:v1.5`
   (768d). The MPE repo is primarily Go, so the build script lives outside the Go module —
   the most pragmatic option is a small Python script (since the ML/embedding ecosystem is
   concentrated there) invoked from the GH Action, calling Ollama's HTTP API rather than
   loading a model in-process. GH Actions runs a local Ollama instance to serve embeddings;
   no customer-infra runtime dependency.
3. Build a lexical index (BM25-style; in-memory, no ES) over the same chunks in the same
   Python step and serialize them. Computing once at artifact build time avoids duplicating
   the work on the consumer side.
4. Hand-curate `curated_baseline.md` (~1–2K tokens). This is the only manually-edited
   file in the artifact; everything else is mechanical from the docs source. Curation
   lives in the OSS repo so it is reviewable alongside doc changes — the same PR that
   changes docs should review the baseline for staleness. Format: plain Markdown,
   single file, no frontmatter required, headings optional. Consumers treat it as raw
   text to prepend to the LLM system prompt.
5. Emit `manifest.json` with:
   ```json
   {
     "manifest_version": 1,
     "mpe_version": "...",
     "embed_model": "nomic-embed-text:v1.5",
     "embed_dims": 768,
     "embed_query_prefix": "search_query: ",
     "chunk_count": ...,
     "build_timestamp": "...",
     "doc_commit_sha": "..."
   }
   ```
   `manifest_version` is the contract version for this artifact schema. Consumers must
   hard-error on an unsupported value so the two repos can evolve at different cadences
   without silent breakage. (Implementation note: the shipped `manifest.json` is a superset
   of this — it also carries `embed_model_digest`.)

### Artifact layout (data-only; no code)

```
mpe-knowledge-vX.Y.Z.jar    # zip containing:
  manifest.json
  curated_baseline.md
  chunks.jsonl              # one JSON object per line
  vectors.bin               # float32 packed, row-major, one row per chunk (embed_dims wide)
  lexical-index.bin         # serialized BM25 postings
  META-INF/maven/io/github/manetu/mpe-knowledge/pom.xml
```

Estimated size: 60 files × ~5 chunks × (~1 KB text + 3 KB vector @768d + lexical
posting) ≈ 40–80 MB uncompressed, ~15–25 MB gzipped. Trivial to embed in a container
image.

The artifact is data-only — no Java/Clojure code. All loading and search logic lives in
the consumer (iamlite backend). This keeps the OSS-repo CI language-agnostic
(Python build → zip → jar) and avoids dragging Clojure tooling into the MPE repo.

## Consumer Contract

The following are the stable, versioned interface that consumers may rely on. Everything
else is an internal implementation detail of `build.py` and may change without notice.

| Resource | Format | Guarantee |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | JSON, fields as above | All listed fields present; `manifest_version` increments on breaking changes |
| `curated_baseline.md` | Plain UTF-8 Markdown | No frontmatter; safe to prepend verbatim to an LLM system prompt |
| `chunks.jsonl` | One JSON object per line: `{id, path, heading_path[], text, frontmatter}` | `id` is stable for the same doc commit; `heading_path` is an ordered array of heading strings |
| `vectors.bin` | float32, row-major, `chunk_count × embed_dims` | Row `i` corresponds to chunk `i` in `chunks.jsonl` order; `embed_dims` from manifest |
| `lexical-index.bin` | BM25 postings (format documented below) | Term → posting list mapping over chunk ids |

Consumers **must** validate `manifest_version` before loading. Current supported value: `1`.

### BM25 serialization format

All multi-byte integers and floats are **little-endian**. The file is written
deterministically: vocabulary terms are sorted alphabetically; postings within each term
are sorted by ascending `chunk_id`. Tokenization: `chunk["text"].lower().split()`.

**Header — 16 bytes**

| Offset | Size | Type | Value | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------|-------------|
| 0 | 4 | bytes | `BM25` | Magic number (ASCII) |
| 4 | 2 | uint16 LE | `1` | Format version |
| 6 | 4 | float32 LE | e.g. `1.2` | BM25 k1 parameter |
| 10 | 4 | float32 LE | e.g. `0.75` | BM25 b parameter |
| 14 | 2 | bytes | `\x00\x00` | Reserved, must be zero |

**Vocabulary section** (immediately follows header)

| Field | Size | Type | Description |
|-------|------|------|-------------|
| `vocab_size` | 4 | uint32 LE | Number of unique terms |
| *(repeated `vocab_size` times)* | | | |
| `term_len` | 2 | uint16 LE | Byte length of the UTF-8 term |
| `term` | `term_len` | UTF-8 bytes | The term string |
| `idf` | 4 | float32 LE | IDF score for this term |

**Postings section** (immediately follows vocabulary; same term order)

| Field | Size | Type | Description |
|-------|------|------|-------------|
| *(repeated `vocab_size` times)* | | | |
| `posting_count` | 4 | uint32 LE | Number of documents containing this term |
| *(repeated `posting_count` times)* | | | |
| `chunk_id` | 4 | uint32 LE | 0-based index into `chunks.jsonl` |
| `tf_score` | 4 | float32 LE | BM25 TF component: `freq*(k1+1) / (freq + k1*(1-b+b*|d|/avgdl))` |

**Scoring**: Full BM25 score for query term `q` in document `d` = `idf[q] * tf_score[q][d]`.

**Validation**: Consumers should assert the first 4 bytes equal `BM25` and `version == 1`
before reading further. Hard-error on unknown versions.

## Publishing

**Shipped design (commit `5a48cc9`, superseding the original GitHub-Packages plan below):**
two channels, one workflow:

1. **Clojars** — primary. The GH Action uses `actions/setup-java` + `mvn deploy:deploy-file`
   to push `io.github.manetu:mpe-knowledge:X.Y.Z` to `https://repo.clojars.org/`, authenticated
   via `CLOJARS_USERNAME`/`CLOJARS_PASSWORD` repository secrets. Consumers declare
   `[io.github.manetu/mpe-knowledge "X.Y.Z"]` in their dependency manager. Chosen over GitHub
   Packages because Clojars requires no `read:packages` token for consumer CI or local
   developer machines — public by default, matching the original goal of avoiding auth
   friction, achieved via a different registry rather than a public GH Package.
2. **GH Releases attachment** — mirror, unchanged from the original design. The same workflow
   attaches `mpe-knowledge-vX.Y.Z.jar` to the existing release on
   https://github.com/manetu/policyengine/releases.

<details>
<summary>Original plan (superseded, kept for history)</summary>

~~1. **GitHub Packages (Maven registry)** — primary. The GH Action uses `actions/setup-java`
   + `mvn deploy` to push `com.manetu:mpe-knowledge:X.Y.Z` to
   `https://maven.pkg.github.com/manetu/policyengine`. Standard Maven coordinates;
   consumers declare `[com.manetu/mpe-knowledge "X.Y.Z"]` in their dependency manager.~~

~~Recommend making the GH Package public (if MPE docs are already public) to avoid requiring
a `read:packages` token on consumer CI and local developer machines.~~

</details>

## Implementation

The build pipeline is designed so a single command produces the artifact identically
whether run by GH Actions or by a developer locally. CI is a thin orchestrator over the
same Makefile targets.

### Files to add

```
knowledge/
  build.py            # chunks, embeds, indexes, packs the jar
  curated_baseline.md # hand-curated MPE essentials
  pom.xml             # Maven coordinates: io.github.manetu:mpe-knowledge
  requirements.txt    # pinned Python deps (rank-bm25, python-frontmatter, requests, ...)
  Makefile            # knowledge-build, knowledge-install, knowledge-deploy targets

.github/workflows/publish-knowledge.yml
```

(As shipped: `requirements.txt` has no `sentence-transformers` — embeddings go through Ollama's
HTTP API via `requests`, not an in-process model load.)

### GH Actions workflow

Triggers on release tags. Steps (as shipped):

1. `actions/checkout` (SHA-pinned)
2. `actions/setup-python` (SHA-pinned) → install/start Ollama, pull `nomic-embed-text:v1.5`,
   `make knowledge-build`
3. `actions/setup-java` (Java 17 Temurin; **not yet SHA-pinned** — tracked as a minor
   follow-up, see [[i-4uan]]'s close comment) → `make knowledge-deploy` (`mvn deploy:deploy-file`
   to Clojars, skipped idempotently if the version already exists there)
4. Upload jar as release asset via `softprops/action-gh-release`

CI calls the same `make` targets developers run locally — no duplicated logic.

### Local invocation

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `make knowledge-build` | Creates `knowledge/target/mpe-knowledge-<version>.jar`. Sets up a Python venv on first run, installs from `requirements.txt`, checks a local Ollama server is reachable and has `nomic-embed-text:v1.5` pulled, runs `build.py`. Version from `git describe` (`vX.Y.Z` on a tag, `vX.Y.Z-<sha>-dirty` otherwise) or `MPE_VERSION` env. |
| `make knowledge-install` | Runs `mvn install:install-file` to publish the jar to `~/.m2/repository`. Primary path for day-to-day local development against iamlite. |
| `make knowledge-deploy` | `mvn deploy:deploy-file` to Clojars. Used by CI; developers normally don't run this (requires `CLOJARS_USERNAME`/`CLOJARS_PASSWORD`). |

### Decision points (resolved, as shipped)

- **Embed model:** ~~default suggestion `bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d, ~33 MB, CPU-runnable;
  downloads and caches on first local run)~~ → **shipped as Ollama `nomic-embed-text:v1.5`
  (768d)**, served by a local Ollama daemon rather than an in-process HuggingFace model.
  Rationale: avoids bundling PyTorch/transformers as a Python dependency; Ollama is already
  a common local/CI tool. Trade-off: build reproducibility now depends on a running Ollama
  service rather than a pinned, fully-offline local model (see [[i-3ca4]]'s close comment).
- **Lexical scorer:** BM25 with `k1=1.2, b=0.75` via `rank-bm25`, serialized per the binary
  layout in the Consumer Contract section above — shipped exactly as originally specced.
- **GH Package visibility:** superseded — shipped as **Clojars** (public, no auth needed for
  consumers), not GitHub Packages. See "Publishing" above.

### Determinism

`build.py` should produce byte-identical output (modulo timestamps) for the same doc
commit + same `requirements.txt` lock. Log a sha256 fingerprint of the jar contents
(excluding `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` timestamp bytes) in CI so drift is observable across
builds. **Caveat introduced by the Ollama pivot:** since embeddings are generated by calling
a live Ollama server rather than a pinned local model file, byte-identical `vectors.bin`
output additionally depends on the served model build being identical across runs/machines,
not just on the pinned Python dependency versions.

## Verification

- `make knowledge-build && make knowledge-install` on a clean machine — jar resolves
  locally via `~/.m2`.
- In iamlite, declare `[io.github.manetu/mpe-knowledge "X.Y.Z-local"]` and confirm `lein deps`
  resolves from `~/.m2`; backend boots and `/api/assistant/info` reports the local version.
- Same git commit on two machines (with the same Ollama model build) produces matching jar
  fingerprints.
- `manifest.json` parses and validates: all required fields present, `manifest_version: 1`,
  `chunk_count` matches line count of `chunks.jsonl`, `embed_dims` (768) matches vector row width.

title: notary-verify: offline bundle verifier code review findings
content:
## Context

`notary-verify` adds a new, security-critical Go package (`pkg/audit/verify`) that offline-verifies Manetu audit "verification bundles" — leaf-hash + signature checks, RFC 6962 Merkle inclusion proofs, root-signature/chain-continuity checks, retention-floor evaluation, and optional Rekor/immudb anchor verification — plus a thin CLI wrapper (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify`) and new reference docs (`docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md`, `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md`).

A comprehensive review (5 parallel deep-dives across crypto primitives, anchor verification, orchestration logic, the CLI layer, and docs, plus linting and personal verification of the two highest-severity claims) found that the core cryptography is fundamentally sound — no exploitable *forgery* path exists — but surfaced real gaps in **policy enforcement for multi-record ("set") bundles**, **one genuine Merkle-decoding bug** that will misfire against real-world Rekor logs, and a number of correctness/hygiene/doc-drift issues.

This spec is the umbrella for remediation. Each finding is tracked as its own linked issue (`implements` this spec).

## Fix priority order

1. `--require-anchor` bypass for multi-record bundles (security policy gap)
2. Rekor Merkle inclusion-proof promoted-node bug (breaks real-world use)
3. Nondeterministic root ordering (breaks the "same bytes -> same verdict" invariant)
4. Doc/code drift on bundle schema (misleads implementers on security-relevant fields)
5. Silent-failure CLI output gap on `FloorOK == nil`
6. Remaining medium/low correctness, hygiene, and test-coverage gaps

## Non-goals

- This spec does not cover writing the *notary/producer* side of the bundle format — only the verifier and its CLI/docs.
- Style/lint nitpicks that don't affect correctness or security are tracked but are lowest priority.

## Source

Multi-agent `/code-review` run on branch `notary-verify` vs `main`, 2026-07-16. Reviewed: `pkg/audit/verify/*.go` (+ tests), `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/*.go` (+ tests, parity fixtures), `docs/docs/reference/cli/verify.md`, `docs/docs/reference/verification-bundle-schema.md`, `docs/sidebars.ts`, `docs/cspell.json`.

title: notary-verify round 2: anchor-binding gap and hardening findings
content:
## Context

A second `/code-review` pass on `pkg/audit/verify`/`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` (commit `fa00040`,
already merged) found the core cryptography sound — no record-forgery path — but surfaced a HIGH
design gap in anchor verification: anchor checks (Rekor, immudb) prove an anchor entry is internally
valid, but never bind it to *this bundle's* `signed_root.root_hash_b64`. A handful of correctness,
output-clarity, and test-coverage issues were found alongside it.

This is a **second round**: round 1's umbrella spec [[s-2954]] already tracks 17 issues from the
first `/code-review` pass on this same package, of which several are still open
(`i-6s6o`, `i-76hw`, `i-2aru`, `i-99gt`, `i-5hib`, `i-3e8a`, `i-pwxz`, `i-50v4`, `i-3aqt`, `i-5d8p`,
`i-53d7` — hygiene/docs/test-coverage backlog). None of those overlap this round's findings; they are
left alone and not duplicated here.

**Guiding principle:** both this verifier and the notary producer
(`manetu/mpe-iam-lite`, branch `tamper-resistance`) are under active development. Priority is on
getting the design right, not on preserving compatibility with either side's current state. Where a
fix genuinely belongs in the notary rather than the verifier, it is tracked there instead of faked
here — see the `i-H1b` cross-repo note below.

I inspected the notary source (`mpe-iam-lite@tamper-resistance`) to derive the true anchor formats
rather than guessing:
- **Rekor** (`notary/anchor/rekor.clj`, `notary/rekor/client.clj`): anchors
  `artifact = b64url_decode(signed_root.root_hash_b64)` as a `hashedrekord`; the entry's
  `spec.data.hash.value` = `hex(sha256(root_hash_bytes))`. The notary already enforces this at
  fetch/reuse time via `assert-entry-hash-matches!`/`entry-artifact-hash` — so an offline binding is
  well-defined and implementable in the Go verifier now (see `i-H1a`).
- **immudb** (`notary/anchor/immudb.clj`): key=`root_id`, value=`json/encode(signed_payload)` (via
  cheshire, non-canonical); `entry_hash = sha256(sha256(root_id) || sha256(value_bytes))`. The Go
  verifier cannot reproduce `value_bytes` from bundle-visible fields today — binding is not currently
  feasible offline. This is a notary-side gap; tracked as a new spec in `mpe-iam-lite`
  (`s-xhch`, "Make immudb anchor offline-verifiable against its bundle root") rather than faked here
  (see `i-H1b`).
- Confirmed the **reference `notary/verify.clj` has the identical Rekor-binding gap** as the Go port
  — a shared design gap across both languages, not a Go regression. Noted in `s-xhch` as a companion
  follow-up for that repo.

Linters (`go vet`, `staticcheck`) are clean on the current tree.

## Fix priority order

1. Rekor anchor-root binding (security) — `i-H1a`
2. immudb binding — document the limitation and block on the notary fix (security/docs) — `i-H1b`
3. Set-bundle anchor-status overstatement — `i-M1`
4. Canonical-JSON U+007F parity — `i-L1`
5. Chain-link vacuous-match hardening — `i-L2`
6. `ParseDuration` silent overflow — `i-L3`
7. Exit-code/verdict-line clarity — `i-L4`
8. Test-coverage gaps (ECDSA-P256 bundle test, immudb CLI output test) — `i-L5`

## Non-goals

- Does not cover the notary/producer side beyond documenting the blocking dependency for immudb
  binding — that work is tracked in `mpe-iam-lite` spec `s-xhch` instead.
- Does not re-litigate or duplicate round 1's still-open backlog under [[s-2954]].

## Source

Second multi-agent `/code-review` pass on `pkg/audit/verify` + `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify`
(commit `fa00040`), cross-checked against `mpe-iam-lite@tamper-resistance` notary source
(`notary/anchor/rekor.clj`, `notary/anchor/immudb.clj`, `notary/rekor/client.clj`,
`notary/verify.clj`), 2026-07-16.

title: notary-verify round 3: dispatch-ambiguity, memory-cap, and tail-completeness findings
content:
## Context

A third `/code-review` pass on `pkg/audit/verify` / `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify` (commit `ac82395`,
already merged) — three parallel deep-dives (crypto core: `verify.go`/`merkle.go`/`hash.go`/`keys.go`/
`bytes.go`/`canonical.go`; anchor & parsing layer: `rekor.go`/`immudb.go`/`retention.go`/`jsonutil.go`;
CLI & docs: `core.go`/`output.go`/`verify.md`/`verification-bundle-schema.md`), each briefed on the
full set of round 1 ([[s-2954]]) and round 2 ([[s-9vbo]]) findings so as not to duplicate them.

The core cryptography remains sound — RFC 6962 domain separation, canonical-JSON integer handling,
and integer-overflow guards all held up under adversarial tracing. This round's findings are
concentrated in **bundle-shape dispatch** (a genuinely new "VERIFIED on a tampered bundle" path,
distinct from anything round 1/2 found), **CLI input-handling hygiene**, and **documentation
overclaims** about the immudb anchor's binding strength (a follow-on observation on top of round 2's
`i-H1b`, not a duplicate of it — that issue covers the underlying binding *limitation*; this covers
the godoc/schema-doc *overclaiming a fix for it*).

All six findings below were fixed, tested, and verified (build, `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `gosec`,
`golangci-lint`, and the full test suite including `-race`) in the same session as the review —
each issue is filed already `closed` with its fix, regression test, and verification recorded.

## Fix priority order (as applied)

1. Bundle-type dispatch ambiguity — tampered set data smuggled alongside a genuine single record
   reports VERIFIED (security, HIGH) — [[i-39dv]]
2. CLI file reads bypass the memory-exhaustion cap that stdin already honors (MEDIUM) — [[i-5prr]]
3. Set-bundle tail truncation has no caveat, unlike the existing predecessor-side one (MEDIUM) — [[i-2ldg]]
4. immudb godoc/schema-doc overclaims rekor-equivalent cryptographic binding (LOW) — [[i-7xbs]]
5. canonical.go collapses invalid UTF-8 / lone surrogates to U+FFFD (LOW) — [[i-1dpm]]
6. verify.md omits the always-printed `RESULT:` verdict line from its sample output (LOW) — [[i-4otp]]

## Non-goals

- Does not re-litigate or duplicate round 1's ([[s-2954]]) or round 2's ([[s-9vbo]]) still-open
  backlog (`i-6s6o`, `i-76hw`, `i-2aru`, `i-99gt`, `i-5hib`, `i-3e8a`, `i-pwxz`, `i-50v4`, `i-3aqt`,
  `i-5d8p`, `i-53d7`) — none of this round's findings overlap those.
- Does not attempt the `merkle.go`/`VerifyInclusion` length-guard hardening one reviewer suggested:
  tracing actual callers showed `VerifyRekorInclusion` legitimately passes variable-length raw Rekor
  entry bytes as the "leaf" argument, so a blind 32-byte length check would break real Rekor
  verification. Confirmed non-exploitable as-is; left as a documented non-fix rather than risk a
  regression in signature-verification code for zero present security benefit.

## Source

Three parallel `/code-review` agents (crypto core, anchor & parsing layer, CLI & docs) plus personal
verification of every material finding against the source (direct reads of `merkle.go`, `canonical.go`,
`verify.go`, `bytes.go`, `keys.go`, `retention.go`, `immudb.go`), 2026-07-17.

title: immudb anchor: recompute entry_hash from the bundle's own signed_root (retire root_binding_hash)
content:
## Context

Code-review round 3 ([[s-1y1f]], issue [[i-7xbs]]) found that `anchor_refs.immudb.root_binding_hash`
is an unsigned side-channel field, not a cryptographic binding — it sits *beside* immudb's real proof
chain (inclusion proof → `tx_eH` → signed `tx_hash`) rather than being woven into it, so it only
catches accidental mismatch, never adversarial substitution. `i-7xbs` fixed the docs to stop
overclaiming this; this spec is the follow-on design work to close the underlying gap for real,
per explicit user direction: **the strongest available security design wins, even at the cost of
extra complexity/dependencies** — verbosity/dependency-bloat concerns that led the notary side to
choose the weaker design in `mpe-iam-lite`'s `s-xhch` are explicitly overridden for this redo.

## Design (verified against notary source, `mpe-iam-lite` @ current)

The real fix: make `entry_hash` itself — the value immudb's genuine proof chain actually commits
to — independently recomputable by the verifier from bundle-trusted data, instead of trusting it as
asserted (today, `entry_hash` is read straight from `anchor_refs.immudb.entry_hash` and never
cross-checked against anything).

Both sides already have the needed machinery, because they already do the equivalent operation for
the root *signature*:

- Go: `SignableRootFields` + `selectKeys` + `CanonicalJSONBytes` (`pkg/audit/verify/verify.go`,
  `canonical.go`), used today only by `VerifyRootSignature`.
- Clojure: `signable-root-fields` + `select-keys` + `canonical/canonical-json-bytes`
  (`notary/verify.clj:760-770`, `notary/canonical.clj`), used today only by `verify-root-signature`.

Target formula (mirrors `immudb-entry-hash`'s existing `sha256(sha256(key) || sha256(value))` shape):

```
expected_value_bytes = CanonicalJSONBytes(selectKeys(signed_root, SignableRootFields))
expected_entry_hash  = sha256(sha256(root_id) || sha256(expected_value_bytes))
require expected_entry_hash == anchor_refs.immudb.entry_hash
```

This requires the notary to (a) store the immudb anchor value as
`canonical-json-bytes(select-keys(signed-payload, signable-root-fields))` instead of cheshire's
non-canonical `json/encode(signed-payload)` over the full (superset) payload, and (b) expose
`root_id` on the bundle. Confirmed by reading `notary/anchor/immudb.clj` and `notary/bundle.clj`:
**single-record bundles carry no `root_id` field anywhere today** — `assemble-record-bundle` uses
`root-id` only internally to fetch the root/anchor entries, never serializes it. Set bundles already
expose it for free, as the `signed_roots`/`anchor_refs_by_root` map keys.

Also confirmed `root_id = base64url(sha256(kind || partition(4BE) || from_seq(8BE) || to_seq(8BE)))`
(`persistence/driver/notary/batcher.clj`'s `compute-root-id`) is *not* safely re-derivable by the
verifier from bundle-visible fields alone: `kind` ("batch" vs "heartbeat") is not reliably
distinguishable from `covered_range` alone (a genuine single-record batch and a heartbeat can share
identical `from_seq`/`to_seq`). Baking that ambiguity into a security check is exactly the kind of
fragility this redo should avoid — so `root_id` must be an explicit bundle field, not reconstructed.

## Cross-repo dependency

This repo's issues below are inert until the companion notary-side work lands in `mpe-iam-lite`
(new spec, created separately there — not linkable cross-repo from this tool, referenced here by
description only): expose `root_id` on single-record bundles, switch the immudb anchor value to the
canonical `signable-root-fields` encoding, update `notary/verify.clj`'s own `verify-immudb-anchor` to
perform the same recomputation, and retire `root_binding_hash` entirely. Per explicit user direction,
**no backward compatibility is required** — this is a coordinated, all-at-once cutover; anchors
written before it simply fail the strengthened check after, which is acceptable.

## Supersedes / relates to

- [[i-7xbs]] (this repo, closed) — corrected the docs' false equivalence claim; this spec is the
  actual cryptographic fix for the limitation those docs described.
- [[s-9vbo]] / its issue `i-H1b` (this repo) — round 2's original tracked limitation ("immudb anchor
  cannot be bound to the bundle root offline — document limitation, block on notary fix"). This spec
  closes it for real instead of leaving it as a documented, accepted limitation.
- `mpe-iam-lite`'s `s-xhch` (implemented as `root_binding_hash` via its issues `i-n0va`/`i-41py`/
  `i-60zh`) — `s-xhch`'s own analysis already identified a stronger "raw value passthrough" family of
  fix and rejected it for verbosity/dependency-bloat. This spec revisits that call with a leaner
  variant (reusing existing canonical-JSON/signable-fields infrastructure already used for the root
  signature, rather than adding raw-value passthrough + in-verifier JSON parsing) and supersedes
  `root_binding_hash` outright rather than extending it.

## Fix priority order

1. (tracked in `mpe-iam-lite`, not this repo) Notary schema/logic changes: expose `root_id` on
   single-record bundles; change the immudb anchor value encoding; update `verify.clj`.
2. This repo: recompute `entry_hash` from the bundle's own `signed_root` + `root_id`; retire
   `root_binding_hash` — [[i-4spt]]
3. This repo: schema/CLI docs — reflect new `root_id` field, retired `root_binding_hash` — [[i-h9bz]]
4. This repo: regression tests (mismatched-root anchor must fail) + retire `root_binding_hash`-specific
   tests — [[i-8vz7]] — and regenerate cross-repo parity fixtures once the notary ships the new
   format — [[i-1cpa]].

## Non-goals

- Does not preserve verifiability of anchors written before the cutover (explicit user direction).
- Does not touch Rekor's binding (already sound and closed — round 1's `i-2jp1`).

## Source

User-directed design review following code-review round 3 (commit `ac82395`) finding `i-7xbs`;
cross-repo source verification against `mpe-iam-lite` (`notary/canonical.clj`, `notary/verify.clj`,
`notary/anchor/immudb.clj`, `notary/bundle.clj`, `persistence/driver/notary/batcher.clj`), 2026-07-17.

title: notary-verify round 4: set-bundle redaction bypass, CLI exit-code/hint, and hygiene findings
content:
## Context

A comprehensive `/code-review` pass on `pkg/audit/verify` / `cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify`
(commit `0101f2f`, "feat(verify): add offline audit bundle verification") — five parallel
deep-dives (crypto primitives: `canonical.go`/`hash.go`/`merkle.go`/`bytes.go`/`keys.go`/
`jsonutil.go`; core orchestration: `verify.go`/`retention.go`/`doc.go`; anchor verification:
`rekor.go`/`immudb.go`; CLI: `core.go`/`output.go`/`main.go`; tests & docs) — each briefed on the
full set of round 1 ([[s-2954]]), round 2 ([[s-9vbo]]), and round 3 ([[s-1y1f]]) findings so as not
to duplicate them. `go vet` and `staticcheck` are clean; the full test suite passes.

The core cryptography remains sound — no record-forgery or signature-bypass path exists. Signatures
bind to the positive `SignableRootFields` allowlist, RFC 6962 domain separation is correct, keys are
always caller-supplied (never read from the bundle), and both Rekor and immudb anchors genuinely bind
to the bundle's own root hash. All prior rounds' critical/high fixes are present with regression
tests.

This round's headline is one **genuinely new HIGH-severity defect**, empirically reproduced: for a
multi-record ("set") bundle, `verifyMultiRecord` never checks that the disclosed `records` actually
cover every leaf the root's own **signed** `tree_size` claims. An assembler can drop an individual
record from an otherwise genuine, correctly-signed, correctly-chained batch and the verifier still
reports `SetComplete` / `ExitCode 0` — the exact "verified for something unproven" failure this tool
exists to prevent. This is distinct from prior findings:
- **not** closed `i-4mfr` (density check = `tree_size` vs `covered_range` **span**);
- **not** closed `i-2ldg` (unsigned **tail** boundary `completeness.to_seq`, i.e. records dropped
  *past* the bundle's self-asserted end). Round 4's gap is an **interior** redaction *within* a
  cryptographically-signed `tree_size` — the signed evidence is sufficient to catch it but is never
  used for a leaf-coverage count.

The remaining findings are three mediums (a CLI exit-code contract violation, an invalid `rekor-cli`
hint, and unsanitized bundle strings reaching the terminal) and a tail of low/hygiene/test-coverage
items.

## Fix priority order

1. Set-bundle interior-redaction bypass — disclosed records not counted against signed `tree_size`
   (security, HIGH) — [[i-8sjb]]
2. Non-numeric `--trusted-now` exits 1 (collides with the TAMPERED exit code) instead of documented
   3 (MEDIUM) — [[i-2kth]]
3. Rekor hint emits `rekor-cli verify --log-index`, which `rekor-cli verify` rejects (MEDIUM) —
   [[i-z9rk]]
4. Unsanitized bundle strings (`record_id`, `root_hash_b64`) written to stdout — terminal-escape
   spoofing of an operator's view (LOW/MEDIUM, security) — [[i-33dl]]
5. Dead exported API `GenesisSeal`/`ChainSeal`/`ValidSeal` (LOW) — [[i-45eo]]
6. `verify.md` says "schema v1.1" but fixtures/schema ship `1.0` (LOW, docs) — [[i-46g5]]
7. `retention_floor_ms` missing the "advisory only" caveat its sibling fields carry (LOW, docs) —
   [[i-84pn]]
8. `rekor-verified` parity fixture now expects failure — misnamed (LOW, testing) — [[i-8pdd]]
9. No dedicated `jsonutil_test.go` (LOW, testing) — [[i-4u2g]]
10. Missing malformed-base64 decode-error tests for rekor/immudb fields (LOW, testing) — [[i-6xaf]]
11. `rekorAuditPath` lacks an explicit `logIndex` bounds check (LOW, hygiene) — [[i-j03y]]
12. `longToBEBytes` non-negative invariant not enforced at immudb call sites (LOW, hygiene) —
    [[i-8szv]]
13. No `t.Parallel()` across either verify test package (INFO, testing) — [[i-4mdo]]

## Non-goals

- Does not re-litigate or duplicate the still-open backlog from rounds 1–3 ([[s-2954]], [[s-9vbo]],
  [[s-1y1f]]): `i-6s6o`, `i-76hw`, `i-2aru`, `i-99gt`, `i-5hib`, `i-3e8a`, `i-pwxz`, `i-50v4`,
  `i-3aqt`, `i-5d8p`, `i-53d7`, `i-4spt`. Several reviewers independently re-derived items already
  tracked there (e.g. `InclusionProof`/`Root` panic hardening = `i-50v4`); those are left alone.
  Note `i-2kth` is *not* a duplicate of `i-3e8a` (which is about `--trusted-now 0` vs unset); this is
  a *non-numeric* value hitting the framework parser and exiting 1.
- **Ruled out — deep-nesting JSON DoS.** One reviewer flagged `DecodeBundle`
  (`pkg/audit/verify/jsonutil.go`) as lacking a nesting-depth guard, positing a stack-overflow crash
  on a small deeply-nested bundle (per the historically-unresolved golang/go#31789). Refuted on the
  shipped toolchain: this repo builds on `go1.26.0`, whose `encoding/json` enforces a depth limit. A
  10 MB file of nested brackets, run through the real `mpe verify` binary, produced a clean
  `exit 3` ("invalid character '[' exceeded max depth") — no crash, no hang. No issue filed. Latent
  caveat only: the mitigation is toolchain-provided, so a build on a pre-1.26 Go would reintroduce
  the exposure.

## Source

Five parallel `/code-review` agents (crypto primitives, core orchestration, anchor verification, CLI,
tests & docs) plus personal empirical verification of the two highest-stakes claims against a built
`mpe` binary and a throwaway in-package probe test:
- dropping one record from a `buildSetBundle` `tree_size=2` batch → `VerifyBundle` returns
  `SetStatus="complete"`, `ExitCode=0`, all remaining records "verified" (confirms [[i-8sjb]]);
- `mpe verify --trusted-now notanumber …` → exit 1, not the documented 3 (confirms [[i-2kth]]);
- deep-nested-JSON bundle → clean exit 3, no crash (refutes the DoS claim above).

2026-07-17.

title: immudb EnumerateRootsInWindow: implement or retract the claimed prev_root_id chain-walk fallback
content:
## Context

Review of mpe-iam-lite's tamper-resistance branch (cross-session request, 2026-09-09).
`pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go`'s `EnumerateRootsInWindow` (`immudb.go:483-508`) queries the untrusted
SQL discovery-index table `notary_root_index` (`immudb.go:43`) via `rootsInWindow`, then fetches
and JSON-decodes each hit via `verifiableGet`. Its own comment (`immudb.go:475-482`) claims:

> "the prev_root_id chain always recovers full enumeration by walking backward from AnchorHead"

Confirmed by direct inspection (2026-09-09): the function body implements no such walk — it is a
straight-line query-then-fetch with no chain traversal at all. If `notary_root_index` ever has a
row silently missing (a real, independently-tracked bug on the mpe-iam-lite side: the write path
populating this same table sometimes swallows a write failure — see mpe-iam-lite sudocode spec
`s-7ykm`), the missing root simply doesn't appear in the enumerated result. Today that surfaces as
a `chain`/`contiguity` finding (per `scan.go`'s prev-comparison walk) for a root that was never
actually tampered with — a **false tamper-evidence finding**, because nothing here can currently
distinguish "index bookkeeping gap" from "genuinely withheld root."

## Decision needed: implement vs. retract

Either:

(a) **Implement** the `prev_root_id`-walk-from-`AnchorHead` fallback the comment already claims
    exists, or
(b) If the decision is not to implement it, **correct the comment** at `immudb.go:475-482` to stop
    asserting a capability that doesn't exist.

## Constraints if implementing (a) — security-load-bearing, not optional

A naive implementation can silently turn this into a gap-suppression mechanism, which would be a
real security regression, not just a missing feature:

1. **Independently re-verify** any walked-to candidate root (signature, anchor-inclusion) before
   trusting it — never accept it purely on the walk's say-so.
2. If the walk reaches a candidate root-id (named by a neighbor's own `prev_root_id`) and the
   fetch returns not-found, that is **genuine absence, not a bookkeeping gap**, and MUST still
   surface as a hard finding — ideally sharpened to say specifically "predecessor root-id X does
   not exist in the anchor's verified store," distinguishable from a recovered index-only gap.
   Silently treating a dead end as "recovered, move on" would hide real tamper evidence — do not
   do this.
3. **Bound the walk** — only trigger it when the SQL-derived enumeration already looks incomplete
   relative to `AnchorHead` (don't run it on every scan); cap how far back it walks, mirroring the
   existing `immudbMaxWindowRoots`-style guard already in this file (`immudb.go:463-465`).

## Non-goal

`s3.go`'s enumeration has no analogous fragility — no separate discovery index; enumeration is
derived directly from WORM object keys. Scope this to immudb only.

## Regression tests to specify

(a) Remove/corrupt a `notary_root_index` row for an otherwise durably-anchored root — assert the
    fallback recovers it and reports no finding.
(b) Remove the row **and** the root's own verified-KV entry — assert the fallback still reports
    the same class of finding the scanner produces today (not a silent pass).

## Cross-repo reference

References mpe-iam-lite sudocode spec `s-7ykm` ("immudb anchor discovery-index write is not
durable, contrary to its own design record") — it tracks the write-side bug and this repo's own
(separately dormant, non-production-path) Clojure implementation of the same fallback. Per the
requesting session, `s-7ykm` will be updated to reference this spec back once filed. Cross-repo
graph linking isn't available from this tool; this is a textual reference only.

## Source

Cross-session review request (session `notary-branch-review-findings`) reviewing mpe-iam-lite's
tamper-resistance branch, 2026-09-09. Claims independently verified against current
`pkg/audit/scan/immudb.go` (lines 43, 463-465, 475-508) before this spec was filed.

title: scan: interior-gap seam-localization test coverage + Kafka-retention doc accuracy check
content:
## Context

Review of mpe-iam-lite's tamper-resistance branch (cross-session request, 2026-09-09) found a
test-coverage gap in `pkg/audit/scan/scan_test.go`. The three existing gap-flavored cases —
`TestScanContiguityGapIsFinding`, `TestScanTailTruncationIsFinding`,
`TestScanWholePartitionDropIsFinding` — each mutate a `covered_range` field or drop a whole
partition. None removes an interior root from `fakeAnchorClient`'s `windows` map (the
`EnumerateRootsInWindow` fake, `fakes_test.go:44-56`) to test seam-localization directly.

`scan.go:100-173`'s chain/contiguity walk only ever compares `prev` — the *previously enumerated*
root — to the current one (`prev` assigned at line 172, checked at lines 121 and 148). When an
interior root is silently missing from the enumerated slice (as opposed to a mutated field on a
root that IS present), the walk should still produce exactly one localized `chain`/`contiguity`
finding at the seam where the gap is, and every root after the seam should continue to scan clean
(no cascading findings). This is the exact mechanism a corrupted/omitted discovery-index row would
trigger in production — see [[s-5910]], which covers the immudb-specific case where the missing
root is a bookkeeping gap rather than genuine tamper. Verified today only indirectly, never with a
test that removes an element from the fake's return.

## Design

Add a new test, `TestScanInteriorRootGapIsLocalizedFinding`, alongside the existing gap-flavored
cases in `scan_test.go`, using the `fakeAnchorClient` pattern from `fakes_test.go`:

- Build a chain of >=3 signed roots (root-0, root-1, root-2) via the existing batch-building
  helpers, anchored in `anchor.windows[0]`.
- Remove the *interior* root (root-1) from the slice before scanning — an actual element removal,
  not a field mutation — so `EnumerateRootsInWindow` returns `[root-0, root-2]`.
- Run `Scan` and assert:
  - Exactly one `chain` (and/or `contiguity`, depending on which check trips first per `scan.go`'s
    per-root ordering) finding is reported, anchored to root-2 (the root immediately after the
    gap), matching the seam-localization the algorithm's `prev`-only-compares-to-previous design
    implies.
  - No finding is reported against root-0 (before the gap).
  - `result.ExitCode == 2`.

## Doc/comment accuracy pass (scoped to `pkg/audit/scan/` and `pkg/audit/verify/`)

Confirmed by direct inspection (2026-09-09): nothing in either package implies Kafka retention on
mpe-iam-lite's `accesslog-notary-roots` topic affects completeness scanning. `doc.go:5-14` states
the scanner "dials the configured anchor backend (S3 or immudb) directly" with no Kafka
dependency. Repo-wide grep of `pkg/audit/` for `kafka`/`Kafka` returns only two incidental phrase
hits (`verify.go:127` "Kafka offset", `types.go:26` "Kafka covered_range sequence position") — not
an actual dependency. No inaccurate claim exists today; this task is to keep that confirmation on
record and re-check if either file changes before this issue closes, since `s-59k4` (see below) is
actively changing retention semantics on the notary side while this issue is open.

## Cross-repo reference

This corresponds to mpe-iam-lite sudocode spec `s-59k4` ("Simplify accesslog-notary-roots
retention: delivery buffer, not evidentiary artifact"), which does the retention-simplification
work on that side. Cross-repo graph linking isn't available from this tool; this is a textual
reference only.

## Non-goals

- Does not implement the immudb chain-walk fallback — tracked separately in [[s-5910]].
- Does not change `scan.go`'s algorithm — this is test-coverage + doc-accuracy only.

## Source

Cross-session review request (session `notary-branch-review-findings`) reviewing mpe-iam-lite's
tamper-resistance branch, 2026-09-09. Claims independently verified against current
`pkg/audit/scan/scan.go`, `scan_test.go`, `fakes_test.go`, `doc.go` before this spec was filed.

title: notary-verify round 4: mpe verify tamper-evidence tooling — fail-open findings in scan/verify
content:
## Context

`/code-review` of commit `010dee2` ("feat(verify): add mpe verify audit tamper-evidence tooling") on
branch `tamper-evidence` — the commit that introduced `mpe verify record` (`pkg/audit/verify`, offline
bundle verifier) and `mpe verify completeness` (`pkg/audit/scan`, online anchor-authoritative
completeness scan) into the Community CLI.

This is round 4 in the `notary-verify` review lineage (`s-2954` round 1, `s-9vbo` round 2, `s-1y1f`/
`s-16qk` round 3, `s-5910` round 3.5). Unlike prior rounds, this one covers two packages at once
because `pkg/audit/scan` did not exist before this commit.

**Overall verdict: request changes.** `pkg/audit/verify` (the offline verifier) is excellent — correct
domain separation, canonical-JSON byte-matched against the actual Jackson signer, exemplary negative
tests on the immudb path — and has a small number of real bugs. `pkg/audit/scan` (the completeness
scan) is not ready: seven of its checks can be defeated without producing a finding, and its immudb
tier cannot pass against a real server. Mechanical baseline (`go vet`, `golangci-lint`, `staticcheck`,
`gosec`, `go test -race`) is clean throughout; every finding here is a design/logic gap, not something
a linter would catch.

Review method: two dimensions reviewed in parallel (`pkg/audit/scan` end-to-end; CLI wrappers + docs +
`pkg/audit/verify` output fidelity), every finding independently re-verified against the actual code
before being written up here. Two findings (the immudb `entry_hash` formula, and `authorized_absent`'s
trust model) were additionally cross-checked against the live `mpe-iam-lite` notary source
(`/Users/ghaskins/sandbox/git/mpe-iam-lite`, branch `tamper-resistance`, commit `796d7d3`,
2026-09-09) — see the cross-repo section below for what that confirmed.

## Guiding principle (carried from s-9vbo/s-16qk)

Both this verifier and the notary producer (`mpe-iam-lite`) are under active development. Priority is
on getting the design right, not preserving compatibility with either side's current state. Where a
fix genuinely belongs in the notary rather than this verifier, say so rather than faking a
verifier-side workaround.

## Findings, most severe first

Each heading below is this spec's own short-code; see "Linked issues" at the end for the real
sudocode issue id backing it.

### High — `pkg/audit/scan` (the completeness scan can be defeated)

**S1** ([[i-5dnn]]) — immudb `entry_hash` formula in `scan/immudb.go`'s `immudbHTreeLeaf`/`AnchorRef` is
the formula `pkg/audit/verify` itself documents as disproven (`sha256(sha256(key)||sha256(value))`
over raw stored bytes, missing the real HTree leaf's `0x00`/mdLen/kLen construction); step 3
(anchor-inclusion proof) fails on every root against a real immudb server. Already independently
discovered and orphaned — see `i-5j2n`'s closing feedback (2026-09-09), which recommended a dedicated
follow-up spec that was never filed; this is that follow-up. **Confirmed fixable now, Go-side only**:
read live `mpe-iam-lite` source directly — `notary/canonical.clj`'s `signable-root-bytes` is
`canonical-json-bytes(select-keys(payload, signable-root-fields))`, the same 10-field list as Go's
`SignableRootFields`, and `notary/anchor/immudb.clj`'s `append-root!` writes exactly this narrowed
value as the KV entry. The `s-16qk` notary-side cutover has landed. `verify/immudb.go`'s
`expectedImmudbEntryHash` (signable-subset-only) is therefore confirmed correct; `scan/immudb.go`'s
formula is confirmed wrong — a straightforward "didn't get the fix `pkg/audit/verify` got," not a
design ambiguity. Fix: delete `immudbHTreeLeaf`, reuse `verify`'s implementation (already exported via
`ImmudbALHFields`). Add one test driving a canned real-gateway `verifiable/get` response end-to-end
through `VerifyAnchorProof`. Fix the stale doc at `verify/immudb.go:22-23` (still states the retired
formula).

**S1b** ([[i-kd5t]]) (new, surfaced by the cross-repo check above, tracked separately since it's
blocked on different work) — independent of S1's formula bug, `scan.go`'s step 2a
(`VerifyRootSignature(root.Payload, ...)`, `scan.go:108`) is *unconditionally* broken against the
immudb tier for a second reason: immudb's anchored KV value never carries `root_signature_b64` at all
— confirmed by design, not oversight, in both `notary/anchor/immudb.clj` and
`persistence/driver/notary/signed_root_index.clj`, whose own docstring says "immudb narrows its
anchored value to the canonical signable fields, so it cannot serve the full payload back on a cold
read." The notary's answer for the *offline bundle-assembly* path is a separate, non-authoritative
Elasticsearch read-model (`signed_root_index`, populated by the `LeafIndexMaterializer`) that
`notary/bundle.clj` consults for the full signed root — but this read-model is **not exposed to the
online completeness scanner at all**: checked `notary_rest.clj`, whose only consumer of
`signed-root-index/get-signed-roots` is internal, inside `record-existence-rows`, solely to compute
`authorized_absent` server-side. No REST endpoint serves a full signed root (with signature) to the Go
scan client for the immudb tier. **Blocked on new notary-side work** (a `mpe-iam-lite` endpoint
exposing `signed_root_index` to the online scanner) before this can be fixed Go-side.

**S2** ([[i-8qux]]) — `authorized_absent` (`scan.go:254`) is taken on faith from the audited service
with zero independent recomputation; `Config.TrustedNowMs` is plumbed in from `--trusted-now` and
never read anywhere in `pkg/audit/scan`, even though `verify.AuthorizedFloor` is exported and the
root's signed `retention_policy` is already in hand. Failure scenario: deployment runs
`retention_policy = {"mode":"retain-all"}` (floor 0, every record must be present); attacker deletes a
record and has the proxy answer `authorized_absent: true`; scan reports zero findings, exit 0, despite
the root's own signed policy making that logically impossible. **Independently confirmed at the
source**: `notary_rest.clj`'s `record-existence-rows` computes `authorized_absent` via
`(verify/retention-floor-ok? notary-ts-to retention-policy (System/currentTimeMillis))` — the *notary
service's own wall clock*, with no hash or signature covering the result at all. Unlike every other
field this endpoint returns (genuinely self-authenticating, per `doc.go`'s claim), `authorized_absent`
is a bare, unsigned server assertion by design — the scanner's own recomputation is the *only* possible
check on it, not an optional hardening. Fix: compute
`floor, err := verify.AuthorizedFloor(rp, cfg.TrustedNowMs)` from the root's signed `retention_policy`;
reject `authorized_absent == true` whenever `root.notary_ts_to >= floor`; fail closed on `err`.

**S3** ([[i-2704]]) — record-existence rows (`scan.go:250`) are reconciled against what the server
*returned* (`for _, row := range rows`), never against what was *requested* (`ids`); an omitted row is
a silent pass. `NotaryClient.RecordExistence` doesn't check coverage either. Directly falsifies the
package's own stated threat model (`doc.go:11-14`, `notary_client.go:19-23`: "a compromised service can
only omit rows, which the scan's density/existence checks already catch" — omission is exactly what
isn't caught). Unrepresentable in the current test harness: `fakes_test.go:97` always emits one row per
requested id. Fix: `pending := set(ids)` per chunk, delete on each row received, emit a
`record-existence` finding for every id still pending.

**S4** ([[i-713y]]) — `found: true` (`scan.go:251-252`) is accepted without binding to the
anchor-verified leaf; `RecordExistenceRow.LeafHashB64`/`.SignatureB64` are populated by the client and
never read by any non-test code — the exact self-authenticating fields collected for this purpose are
discarded. Failure scenario: attacker deletes a record, proxy answers `found:true, leaf_hash_b64:"",
signature_b64:""`; scan `continue`s. Fix: require `row.LeafHashB64 == leaf.LeafHashB64` and verify
`row.SignatureB64` over that leaf hash with `cfg.NotaryPubKey`.

**S5** ([[i-6mjb]]) — a total window wipe (every requested partition returns zero roots) defeats step
6's own whole-window-wipe branch (`scan.go:342-364`), because `maxPartCount` is derived only from
`partition_count` on roots that were *actually enumerated* (`scan.go:103`): if none were, it stays 0
and the loop never runs. Failure scenario (the common single-partition deployment): attacker
delete-markers every root object in the window; enumeration returns `[]`; every downstream step is a
no-op; output reads `0 roots, 0 leaves (idle)` / exit 0, though every record in the window is gone.
`TestScanWholePartitionDropIsFinding` only covers the case where *another* partition survived to
attest `partition_count`. Fix: iterate `requested ∪ [0, maxPartCount)`, not just `[0, maxPartCount)`.

**S6** ([[i-445u]]) — step 5's tail check (`scan.go:184-198`) compares only `to_seq`, never the head's
root id, so a withheld tail *heartbeat* (which re-asserts the predecessor's `to_seq` by construction)
is invisible — the code's own doc comment states the intended invariant ("must actually BE the head")
but the implementation only checks `lastToSeq < head.ToSeq`. `immudb.go:608-619` gets this right
elsewhere in the same file. Fix: when the head is inside the window, also require
`last.RootID == head.RootID`.

**S7** ([[i-3n7f]]) — the anchor head pointer is unauthenticated (S3's is a plain `GetObject` of a
mutable object, no WORM/checksum/signature; immudb's discards every proof field from `verifiableGet`),
and S3's parse (`s3.go:126-132`) discards ok-flags, so a malformed/legacy `latest.json` yields a
non-nil, all-zero `AnchorPointer` whose `NotaryTsTo == 0` makes step 6 (`scan.go:358`) classify a
wiped partition as idle — the opposite of the "more cautious, never less" claim the code comments make
(true for step 5, false for step 6, added later). Combined with S5, a legacy pointer plus a
full-window delete scans clean. Fix: error on an absent `root-id`/`to-seq`; treat `NotaryTsTo == 0` as
unknown and force the step-6 check; verify the immudb head entry with `verify.VerifyImmudbAnchor` using
proof material already returned.

### High — `pkg/audit/verify`

**V1** ([[i-62zc]]) — set-bundle chain walk (`verifyMultiRecord`, `verify.go:649-690`) sorts every
root into one global list and requires strict hash-chain adjacency between consecutive entries, with
no check that the two roots *claim* adjacency (`prev_root_id`) and no grouping by
`signed_root.partition`. Neither assumption holds for a real set bundle: `verify_result_set` accepts
up to 500 arbitrary record ids (non-adjacent batches), and root chains are per-partition (the S3 key is
`roots/<partition>/<root_id>.json`; `scan.go:125` gates on adjacency correctly, this code doesn't).
Failure scenario: an auditor verifies a legitimate bundle spanning two non-adjacent batches or two
partitions; every record and every root signature verifies; the tool reports
`Chain continuity: FAIL`, exit 1 — tampering where none exists. Contradicts the documented contract
(`cli/verify.md:167-169`: a non-embedded predecessor is CAVEAT, not FAIL) and re-introduces the
completeness verdict the schema doc explicitly retired for set bundles. Fix: group `sortedRoots` by
partition; within a group, compare only pairs that claim adjacency
(`nextR.prev_root_id == prevR.id`) — a non-adjacent/cross-partition pair contributes `ChainCaveat`, not
`ChainFailed`; keep the existing `prevHash == ""` fail-closed guard for a genuine same-`prev_root_id`
mismatch.

### Medium

**M0** ([[i-316p]]) — the i-33dl ANSI-injection sanitization fix doesn't cover `ChainDetail`
(`output.go:141`, sourced from bundle-controlled `prev_root_id`) or any `AnchorCmds` value
(`output.go:180-190`, built from bundle-controlled `bucket`/`key`/`version_id`/`database`) — both
interpolate unsanitized while `RecordID` and the root-hash hint are correctly sanitized a few lines
away. A crafted control-sequence value in either field can rewrite/hide prior terminal output
regardless of whether the record itself verified. No existing test covers this path. Fix: route both
through the existing `sanitizeForDisplay`.

**M0b** ([[i-89ds]]) — set bundles print nothing when every root's anchor check is `Skipped`
(`verify.go:706-717,731-742` set `Result.ImmudbResult`/`S3Result` to `nil`), while a single-record
bundle in the identical all-skipped scenario always prints an explicit `SKIPPED` line
(`verify.go:431-432,459-460` always populate a non-nil result) — the code comment's "matching the
prior single-root-bundle behavior" claim is false. Fix: populate a `Skipped` result instead of `nil`
in the all-skipped case.

**M1** ([[i-6o6j]]) — set-bundle `record_id` (`verify.go:526-559`) is a display label never bound to
`record_pb_b64`, the leaf hash, or the signature — the only things the cryptographic verdict actually
covers. A bundle producer can relabel which `record_id` is shown next to which genuinely-verified
record, so "is record X intact?" is never actually answered by the tool's own identity check. The repo
now has the `AccessRecord` proto (added in `16ce016`); decoding `record_pb_b64` and comparing its own
id is feasible.

**M2** ([[i-24nc]]) — S3 leading-edge root deletion is explicitly called out in a `scan.go:116-120`
code comment as "a caveat, not a failure" (both chain and contiguity checks are `if prev != nil`-
guarded, so the first enumerated root's own claimed predecessor is never checked), but no caveat is
ever recorded in `Finding`, `PartitionSummary`, or `Result` — the operator sees a clean `RESULT: OK`
with no signal the leading edge was unverified. The immudb client closes this hole elsewhere in the
same package (`immudb.go:644-652` walks `prev_root_id` backward); the S3 client has no equivalent, so
the two tiers give materially different assurance under the same reported verdict.

**M3** ([[i-1s8z]]) *(reported by delegated review, not independently re-verified by the coordinating
pass)* — unbounded reads (`io.ReadAll` with no `io.LimitReader`) on every S3/immudb network response,
and no `Timeout` on either constructed `http.Client`; a hostile or wedged endpoint can OOM or hang the
scan indefinitely.

**M4** ([[i-7d8s]]) *(reported, not independently re-verified)* — `PartitionSummary.HeadOutsideWindow`
is computed and asserted in tests but never rendered by `printResult`, so "step 5's tail check could
not be evaluated for this window" is invisible to an operator; separately, a partition attested by
`partition_count` but not in `--partitions` is silently out of scope with no auto-probe.

### Low / test-quality ([[i-5sz9]] — bundled into one issue, small individually, kept together per
explicit direction to avoid one-issue-per-trivial-item overhead)

- Set-bundle `anchorCmds` (`verify.go:581-588`) ranges a Go map and overwrites by key — nondeterministic
  which of N roots' hint is printed, inconsistent with the surrounding code's explicit determinism
  discipline (`sortedRoots`, a 50-iteration determinism test).
- `state_db`/`database` fallback order is inverted between `verify.go:302-306` and
  `immudb.go:310-313` — the printed hint can name a different DB than the one actually verified.
- `record.integrity.key_id` is parsed into the schema but never compared — a wrong-key scenario reports
  a scary "signature verification failed" instead of a clear "wrong key" diagnostic.
- `DecodeBundle` (`jsonutil.go:20-28`) never checks `dec.More()` — trailing JSON after a valid bundle is
  silently discarded rather than rejected.
- The Merkle "known vector" tests (`merkle_test.go:149-196`) compute expected hashes with the package's
  own `nodeHash`/`leafNodeHash`, so a swapped/omitted domain-separator byte would move both sides of
  every assertion together; one hard-coded published RFC 6962 digest would pin it independently.
- A nil `cfg.Notary`/`cfg.Anchor` panics inside an errgroup goroutine (`scan.go:293`); `Scan` only
  validates `len(cfg.Partitions)`.
- Raw error-body strings are interpolated into CLI-printed errors (`immudb.go:263,359`) without the
  same sanitization `output.go` applies to anchor-sourced display strings.
- `immudbMaxChainWalkSteps = 1_000_000` (`immudb.go:577`) has no cycle detection for a malicious/cyclic
  `prev_root_id` chain; each root also costs two round trips with no caching.
- Not-found classification by substring match (`s3.go:143`, `immudb.go:199-207`) — `"404"` can match
  unrelated transport errors, converting infrastructure failures into tamper findings or vice versa.
- `completeness/config.go:226-229`'s `--immudb-port` uses a zero-value check instead of `cmd.IsSet`,
  the same anti-pattern already fixed for `--trusted-now` elsewhere in this codebase; `--concurrency`/
  `--record-existence-batch-size` remain framework-parsed `IntFlag`s that may share the same
  short-circuit-to-exit-1 issue `record`'s flags were deliberately converted away from — not confirmed
  by execution, worth a quick manual check.
- Several additional **reported-but-not-independently-re-verified** items from delegated review, worth
  triage before acting: enumerated roots' signed `partition`/`notary_ts_to` never cross-checked against
  the partition/window they were enumerated under; `notary_ts_to` ties falling back to `root_id`
  lexical order (uncorrelated with chain order); two disagreeing S3 key parsers silently `continue`ing
  on divergence; the S3 WORM binding never checking the fetched object's bytes decode to the verified
  payload, plus a `retain-all` branch that only accepts a legal hold, not COMPLIANCE-mode retention;
  `ListObjectsV2` pagination able to stall re-listing page 1; `tree_size` never checked against
  `covered_range` span (possibly intentional given legal sparse batches — should be documented either
  way).
- Dependency vulnerabilities (pre-existing, not introduced by this commit): `govulncheck ./...` reports
  19 reachable findings, all in the Go 1.26.0 stdlib or pre-existing `grpc`/`x/net` versions — the two
  modules this commit adds (`aws-sdk-go-v2`, `golang.org/x/sync`) are clean. Worth noting because this
  commit is what first makes `crypto/tls`/`crypto/x509` reachable (via the new S3 client). Track and
  bump separately, not part of this spec's scope.

### Test-quality ([[i-9g08]] — separate issue, the parity-fixture regression is a distinct, focused fix)

The Clojure cross-implementation parity fixtures (`cmd/mpe/subcommands/verify/record/testdata/parity/*`,
`parity_test.go`) are pinned at `schema_version: "1.0"` against `supportedSchemaMajor = "2"`, so all
three (`verified`/`tampered`/`unsealed`) now fail identically at the meta-envelope gate before any
record/signature/Merkle/chain logic runs — the suite no longer distinguishes the three cases at all,
contrary to what its name and the commit message ("with Clojure-parity test fixtures for the record
path") imply. The test's own doc comment discloses this honestly; regenerating schema-2.0 goldens
needs the real Clojure CLI plus a private signing key. Needs either regeneration or an explicit
`t.Skip` with a tracking reference so the suite stops implying a property it no longer tests.
